verses.text: Elisha told the woman whose son he had brought back to life, “Get up and leave with your household. Stay wherever you can, because the LORD has called for a famine, and it will last seven years.”
The woman did what the man of God said. She left with her household and lived in the land of the Philistines for seven years.
When the seven years were over, she returned from Philistine territory and went to ask the king to give her back her house and land.
The king was talking with Gehazi, the man of God's servant. “Tell me about all the great things Elisha has done,” he said.

Just as Gehazi was telling the king how Elisha had brought a dead person back to life, the woman whose son Elisha had restored came to ask for her house and land. Gehazi said, “My lord the king, this is the woman, and this is her son whom Elisha brought back to life.”

The king asked the woman about it, and she told him the story. He assigned an official to her case and said, “Give back everything that belonged to her, including all the produce from her fields from the day she left until now.”
Elisha went to Damascus while Ben Hadad king of Syria was ill. The king was told, “The man of God has come here.”
The king told Hazael, “Take a gift and go meet the man of God. Ask the LORD through him, ‘Will I recover from this illness?’”

Hazael went to meet Elisha, taking gifts of the finest goods in Damascus, as much as forty camels could carry. He stood before him and said, “Your son Ben Hadad king of Syria has sent me to ask, ‘Will I recover from this illness?’”
Elisha told him, “Go tell him, ‘You will surely recover.’ Yet the LORD has shown me that he will surely die.”
Elisha stared steadily at Hazael until Hazael grew uncomfortable. Then the man of God wept.

Hazael asked, “Why are you crying, my lord?” Elisha answered, “I know the terrible things you'll do to Israel. You'll set fire to their strongholds, kill their young men with the sword, dash their little children to pieces, and rip open their pregnant women.”
Hazael said, “How could your servant, a mere dog, do such a thing?” Elisha answered, “The LORD has shown me you'll be king of Syria.”
Hazael left Elisha and went back to his master. Ben Hadad asked, “What did Elisha tell you?” He said, “He told me you'd surely recover.”
The next day Hazael took a thick cloth, soaked it in water, and spread it over the king's face. The king died, and Hazael took his place.
Jehoram son of Jehoshaphat began to rule Judah in the fifth year of the reign of Joram son of Ahab, king of Israel, while Jehoshaphat was still king of Judah.
Jehoram was thirty-two years old when he became king, and he ruled in Jerusalem for eight years.
He followed the ways of the kings of Israel, just as Ahab's family did, because he'd married Ahab's daughter. He did what was evil in the LORD's sight.
Still, the LORD was unwilling to destroy Judah for the sake of his servant David. He had promised that David and his descendants would always have a lamp.
During Jehoram's reign, Edom rebelled against Judah's rule and appointed its own king.
Jehoram crossed over to Zair with all his chariots. The Edomites surrounded him and his chariot commanders, but he rose in the night and struck them. The troops fled to their tents.
Edom has been in rebellion against Judah's rule to this day. Libnah rebelled at the same time.
The rest of Jehoram's acts and everything he did are recorded in the Book of the Chronicles of the Kings of Judah.
Jehoram died and joined his ancestors and was buried with them in David's City. His son Ahaziah became king in his place.
In the twelfth year of the reign of Joram son of Ahab, king of Israel, Ahaziah son of Jehoram became king of Judah.
Ahaziah was twenty-two years old when he became king. He ruled in Jerusalem for one year. His mother was Athaliah daughter of Omri king of Israel.
He followed the ways of Ahab's family and did what was evil in the LORD's sight, just as they did, because he had married into Ahab's family.
Ahaziah went with Joram son of Ahab to fight Hazael king of Syria at Ramoth Gilead. The Syrians wounded Joram.

King Joram went back to Jezreel to recover from the wounds the Syrians had inflicted at Ramah while he was fighting King Hazael. Ahaziah son of Jehoram, king of Judah, went down to visit Joram son of Ahab in Jezreel because he was unwell.
